newsitem.title: UK: Precious Outlook - Gold fragile, eyeing downside.
newsitem.headline: Precious Outlook - Gold fragile, eyeing downside.

text.p: The gold market is braced for further volatility and weakness on Monday after last week's spike higher and subsequent tumble to fresh 3-1/4 year lows.
The downside was open, dealers said, after prices plunged some $14 late last week from a mid-week high above $357 an ounce.
Bullion fixed at a fresh 3-1/4 year low on Friday of $345 an ounce, then sank still further to close at $344.35 in London.
Dresdner Kleinwort Benson bank said in a weekly report that bullion was set for further tests of the downside, with support pegged at $341 and then $335.
Gold might not breach the 1993 low of $326 but the market needed fund support, which was lacking because bonds and shares markets looked more attractive to investors, Dresdner said.
Technical analyst Elli Gifford of Investment Research of Cambridge noted that prices were approaching significant support.

"The February contract is nearing our $342 downside target and, bearing in mind the historic support at $340 on the spot market and the distinctly oversold background, once again it looks worthwhile to book some profits on shorts," Gifford said.
Fears of fresh central bank sales hit an already nervy market mid-week, when dealers noted heavy institutional selling on Wednesday and Thursday.
"No one knows for sure where this big sell-order originated, but it smells like a central bank," a dealer said.
Others said gold producers or large speculative funds could also have been behind the selling.
A spike in near term lease rates pointed to borrowing demand and possible forward selling.
Near-term implied volatilies soared to 13 percent for one-month bids, up from 11 percent last week.
Shadowing gold, platinum tumbled to 3-3/4 year lows on Friday, easily shearing through psychological support at $350 an ounce.
The next support level around $340 could eventually come into play, dealers said.
Silver, a beneficiary of a U.S. fund play on the gold-silver ratio, has shown much greater resiliance than gold.
But it ended last week off its highs on profit-taking, and it could be in for more losses, dealers said.
